messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: bCARMEN (Bacterial Combinatorial Arrayed Reactions for Multiplexed Evaluation of Nucleic acids) - Droplet Microarray CRISPR-Cas13 Detection of Bacterial Species and Antibiotic Resistance Genes

REAGENTS USED:
  - Extracted Bacterial gDNA or Synthetic Target (input nucleic acid, diluted to ~10^3 genome equivalents/copies per uL)
  - PCR Master Mix (Q5 Hot Start polymerase-based, for one-pot multiplexed preamplification)
  - Primer Pool (pooled species-specific or gene-specific primer pairs, total final concentration 3.5 uM)
  - Cas13a Protein (purified Leptotrichia wadei Cas13a, 45 nM final)
  - crRNA Guide (in-vitro transcribed, species- or resistance-gene-specific, 22.5 nM final)
  - Quenched Fluorescent RNA Reporter (RNase Alert v2, 500 nM final)
  - Detection/Nuclease Assay Buffer (40 mM Tris-HCl, 60 mM NaCl, pH 7.3, with 1 mM each ATP/GTP/UTP/CTP, murine RNase inhibitor, and T7 polymerase mix)
  - Fluorescent Barcode Dyes (distinct dye sets for sample droplets and detection-set droplets, 2 uM final)

STEPS:
1. Sample processing and amplification: Perform one-pot, multiplexed PCR preamplification of the target locus (e.g., the topA gene for species identification, or resistance-gene panels) using Q5 Hot Start polymerase with the pooled primer set; run 30 cycles with a 65C annealing temperature.
2. Detection set assembly: Combine purified Cas13a protein, a species/gene-specific crRNA guide, the quenched fluorescent RNA reporter, and nuclease assay buffer (with NTPs, RNase inhibitor, and T7 polymerase mix) to form each detection set.
3. Barcoding: Dilute the amplified target sample and add a distinct fluorescent dye barcode; similarly add a distinct fluorescent dye barcode to each detection set, so that droplet identity (which target or which crRNA guide) can be recovered from color after imaging.
4. Emulsification and pooling: Emulsify each barcoded sample and detection mix into nanoliter droplets; pool equal volumes of all sample droplets and all detection droplets together.
5. Microarray loading: Load the pooled droplet mixture onto a DropArray microfluidic chip containing over 150,000 microwells (each sized to hold two droplets), allowing stochastic pairwise loading so that every target-guide combination is represented across the array.
6. Droplet merging and incubation: Merge the paired droplets in each microwell (e.g., via corona-treater-induced coalescence) to initiate the Cas13 collateral-cleavage detection reaction, then incubate the sealed chip at 37C (imaged at 0, 1, and 3 hour time points).
7. Imaging and readout: Image the microarray using fluorescence microscopy (or, in the droplet-free CARMEN v2 variant, a conventional cell-phone camera under UV illumination) to determine which target-guide well pairs show a positive collateral-cleavage fluorescence signal.
8. Data analysis: Map the premerge barcode identity of each well to its postmerge fluorescence signal to generate a target-by-guide heatmap, calling a well positive when signal exceeds 6 standard deviations above background.

INTERPRETATION: Successful bCARMEN detection is confirmed when the correct target-guide crRNA pair produces a fluorescence signal greater than 6 SD above background with minimal cross-reactivity to non-target species/genes; the paper reports 51/52 (98%) species-specific crRNAs meeting this threshold across a 52-species bacterial panel and 100% (27/27) accuracy for a 14-resistance-gene panel tested on clinical isolates, with a droplet-free CARMEN v2 variant enabling cell-phone-camera readout within approximately 3 hours.

metadata.protocol_name: Multiplexed detection of bacterial nucleic acids using Cas13 in droplet microarrays, bCARMEN (Thakku, Ackerman, Myhrvold, Bhattacharyya, Livny, Ma, Gomez, Sabeti, Blainey & Hung, PNAS Nexus 2022)

sources.title: Multiplexed detection of bacterial nucleic acids using Cas13 in droplet microarrays

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates one representative target-guide-pair reaction from the paper's bCARMEN-Cas13 workflow (Fig. 1: primer/guide design, sample processing and amplification, dropletization of targets and detection sets, loading and imaging of pooled droplets) and the Methods (Nucleic acid amplification, Cas-13 detection reactions, Barcoding/emulsification/droplet pooling, Pooled droplet loading and imaging of microarrays). Because BioScript has no primitive for massively parallel combinatorial droplet pooling or stochastic pairwise microwell loading, the full DropArray step (over 150,000 microwells, each holding 2 droplets, so that every pairwise target-guide combination is represented) is approximated as a single 'mix' of one barcoded sample droplet with one barcoded detection droplet, modeling one target-guide reaction rather than the full combinatorial array. Likewise, BioScript has no primitive for physical droplet-pair coalescence via a corona treater in a sealed microwell; this is folded into the same generic 'mix' operation. The PCR cycle count (30 cycles) and annealing temperature (65C) are paper-confirmed exact values from the Methods (Nucleic acid amplification section). The 37C/3-hour incubation and imaging time points (0, 1, 3 hours) are also paper-confirmed (Pooled droplet loading and imaging of microarrays section), modeled here as a single 180-minute (3-hour) hold rather than three discrete imaging time points, since BioScript has no primitive for imaging at intermediate time points without ending the incubation. Reagent concentrations (45 nM Cas13a, 22.5 nM crRNA, 500 nM RNA reporter, 3.5 uM total primer, 2 uM barcode dye) are taken directly from the Methods but are not encoded as literal concentration values in the .bs file, since BioScript's dispense primitive specifies volume/unit count rather than molar concentration. The final if/else, which disposes the merged-droplet on both the true and false branches, stands in for the paper's actual positive/negative call decision (signal > 6 SD above background), which is determined computationally during downstream image analysis rather than through a differential on-chip action.

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Detection assays were performed with 45 nM purified Leptotrichia wadei Cas13a, 22.5 nM crRNA, 500 nM quenched fluorescent RNA reporter
Amplification was performed by PCR using Q5 Hot Start polymerase with total final primer concentration of 3.5 uM
A total of two microliters of fluorescent dye barcode stocks was added to 18 uL diluted sample mixture or detection mix
chemical_evidence.source_location: Methods, Barcoding, emulsification, and droplet pooling

operation_evidence.source_quote: Unless otherwise stated, 30 cycles of PCR were performed using an annealing temperature of 65C

operation_evidence.bs_operation: merged_droplet = mix barcoded_sample with barcoded_detection for 5s
operation_evidence.source_quote: droplets in each microwell were then merged by passing the tip of a corona treater over the PCR film
operation_evidence.source_location: Methods, Pooled droplet loading and imaging of microarrays

operation_evidence.bs_operation: heat merged_droplet at 37c for 180m / carmen_signal = detect fluorescence
operation_evidence.source_quote: Merged droplets were imaged at 0, 1, and 3 hour time points and incubated in a 37C warm room
operation_evidence.source_location: Methods, Pooled droplet loading and imaging of microarrays

numeric_mismatches.field: single merged_droplet reaction (not full combinatorial array)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper pools droplets and loads them onto a DropArray chip with over 150,000 microwells to represent every pairwise target-guide combination stochastically; BioScript has no primitive for parallel combinatorial pooling/loading, so this .bs file models a single representative target-guide pair reaction rather than the full array.

The paper images merged droplets at 0, 1, and 3 hour time points during the 37C incubation; this is modeled as one continuous 180-minute hold followed by a single detect step, since BioScript cannot image at intermediate points without ending the heat operation.

numeric_mismatches.field: Reagent concentrations (45 nM Cas13a, 22.5 nM crRNA, 500 nM reporter, 3.5 uM primer, 2 uM dye) not encoded numerically
numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript's dispense primitive specifies a volume/unit count, not a molar concentration; these paper-confirmed concentrations inform reagent selection in the .bs file's manifest but are not literally represented as numeric parameters.

Both branches perform the same disposal action because the paper's actual positive/negative call (signal > 6 SD above background) is determined during downstream, off-chip computational image analysis, not through a differential on-chip action.
